record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Continuous-Time Quantum Walks
record.original_question: Given a graph G together with its eigenvalues and eigenspaces, find necessary and sufficient conditions for the continuous-time quantum walk on G to admit instantaneous uniform mixing, that is, for there to exist a time τ such that all entries of U(τ) have the same absolute value, equivalently all entries of M(τ)=U(τ)∘U(-τ) are equal.

evidence.quote: We say that G admits instantaneous uniform mixing (or simply uniform mixing) at time τ if all entries of M(τ) are equal. Equivalently, G admits uniform mixing at time τ if all entries of U(τ) have the same absolute value.
Given the eigenvalues and eigenspaces of a graph, give necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform mixing to occur.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix $A$, and let $A=\sum_{r} \lambda_r E_r$ be its spectral decomposition, where $\lambda_r$ are the distinct eigenvalues and $E_r$ are the orthogonal projections onto the corresponding eigenspaces. The continuous-time quantum walk on $G$ is the one-parameter family of unitary matrices
$$U(t) = e^{itA} = \sum_r e^{it\lambda_r} E_r, \qquad t\in\mathbb{R}.$$
Define the mixing matrix
$$M(t) = U(t)\circ U(-t) = U(t)\circ \overline{U(t)},$$
where $\circ$ is the entrywise (Schur/Hadamard) product; equivalently, $M(t)_{u,v}=|U(t)_{u,v}|^2$. Say that $G$ admits instantaneous uniform mixing at time $\tau$ if every entry of $M(\tau)$ equals $1/|V(G)|$, equivalently if all entries of $U(\tau)$ have the same absolute value.

Problem: In terms of the eigenvalues $\{\lambda_r\}$ and eigenprojections $\{E_r\}$ of $G$, give necessary and sufficient conditions for there to exist a time $\tau\in\mathbb{R}$ at which $G$ admits instantaneous uniform mixing.
artifact.status_search_result: A complete spectral characterization of instantaneous uniform mixing for continuous-time quantum walks on general graphs has not been found. Partial results exist (e.g., characterizations for specific classes such as certain Cayley graphs, circulants, and Hamming graphs, and spectral conditions for the weaker notion of average uniform mixing in reversible Markov chains), but the general necessary-and-sufficient conditions in terms of eigenvalues and eigenspaces remain open.

status_evidence.title: Average Mixing in Quantum Walks of Reversible Markov Chains
status_evidence.snippet: Spectral conditions have been given for average uniform mixing in the continuous quantum walk to occur.
status_evidence.claim: Only average (not instantaneous) uniform mixing has spectral characterizations; instantaneous uniform mixing remains less understood.

status_evidence.title: ϵ-Uniform Mixing in Discrete Quantum Walks
status_evidence.snippet: a characterization of uniform mixing phenomena on regular non-bipartite graphs has been established in terms of their adjacency eigenvalues and eigenprojections
status_evidence.claim: Related characterizations exist for discrete quantum walks on restricted graph classes, but not a general continuous-time result.
